extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, instrument-makers, and members of the Royal Society (17th-century scientists and observers)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and desiderata for the design, construction, and evaluation of astronomical/mechanical instruments (particularly Hooke's new quadrant) and for the applicability of mathematical proportion to practical problems, as discussed in a 17th-century Philosophical Transactions issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sights: discover the minutest part without strain
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments' sights should be such as may be made to discover the minutest part discoverable in an object, not at all straining the eye, and fit for all eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sights must enable the observer to discern the smallest details comfortably; suitability for different observers' vision is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions: match sight resolution down to seconds
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisions should be such as will distinguish the angle as minutely as the sights will distinguish the parts or objects, and that even to seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings/scales on the instrument must be precise enough to take full advantage of the instrument's optical resolution (ideally to arc-seconds where possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-glance co-observation of separated objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Such a contrivance of the sights, that with one glance of the eye, both the objects, though a semi-circle distant, are at once distinguished and seen together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the optical arrangement so widely separated objects can be brought into the field together for direct comparison/measurement in one view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to set instrument exactly perpendicular
rubrics_metrics.description: A method of setting it exactly perpendicular to a second if need be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision for precise orthogonal/alignment adjustment is required to ensure correct orientation relative to reference axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixation and motion to track celestial objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Its fixation and motion; it being so fixed and moved, that if once set to the objects, it continues to move along with them, as long as it is necessary to continue, or be very certain of any observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mounting and drive mechanisms must permit stable tracking of targets so that observations can be maintained accurately over the required interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easy manufacture, adjustment, and robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Its being to be made and adjusted without difficulty, and not to be put out of order without design; as also in its great easiness of being rectified and again adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for practical construction, straightforward routine adjustment/calibration, and resilience against accidental misalignment; must be easy to correct when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affordability (not very chargeable)
rubrics_metrics.description: In its being not very chargeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost should be reasonable so the instrument is not prohibitively expensive to build or maintain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define material terms clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain what is meant by every material word used (such as matter, body, figure, place, motion, quantity, quality, habit, time, proportion, weight, swiftness, force, and elasticity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting theories or applications, supply explicit definitions of key terms to avoid ambiguity in application and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to drawing/driving powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply duplicate (and sub-duplicate) proportion to the drawing or driving powers which force ships or other bodies through the water, with reference to the respective velocities caused thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the square (or related) proportional reasoning to relate driving power and resulting velocities in fluid resistance contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to shape/sharpness effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the shapes or sharpness of bodies cutting or dividing the water, and in the different velocities arising from thence, where the bodies and forces are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate geometric proportions of object cross-section/shape to hydrodynamic velocity effects using duplicate/sub-duplicate relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to strength of timbers/materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the strength of timbers, or other homogeneous materials applied to buildings, to carts, or any other machinery intended for strength: and how by a model to judge the sufficiency of such engine as is represented by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional reasoning to scale models to predict material strength/performance in full-scale constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to oars and vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the effect of oars upon equal and like vessels, according to their numbers, length, blades, and motions, with or against the stream of smooth or uneven waters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate oar geometry and arrangement to vessel propulsion using proportional laws; consider flow conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to horse motion and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the motion or travelling of horses, on their several paces, and with different burthens on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model locomotion and load-bearing performance by proportional relationships between gait, load, and speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to mills and wheel velocity/strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the strength and velocity of mills and their wheels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate wheel size/geometry and input forces to output velocity and mechanical advantage via proportional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to effects of gunpowder
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the effects of gunpowder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional relationships to scale explosive force/effects with respect to charge size and containment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to auditory distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the distance at which sounds may be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model sound propagation intensity/detectability with distance using proportional scaling laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to olfactory distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the distances at which odoriferous matters may be smelt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional reasoning to model dispersion/dilution of volatile substances and detection distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to visual detectability distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the distance at which the objects of sight may be seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate object size/brightness and observer resolution to maximum sighting distance via proportional laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to pendulum return times
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the time of the returns made by vibrating pendulums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate pendulum length/geometry to period using squared (or sub-squared) proportional relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to human life duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the lives of men and their duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional models cautiously to relate factors thought to influence lifespan; context and assumptions must be explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to musical and sounding bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to musical and sounding bodies, such as strings and bells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional relationships between dimensions/tension and frequencies to predict pitch and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to fire and burning spirits
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the effects and motions of fire and burning spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model flame behavior and heat effects in relation to fuel geometry/quantity using proportional reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to rising/falling of bodies (especially water)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the rising and falling of bodies, but especially of water in pumps, overshot mills, leaks in ships, the heights of rivers at their head above their fall into the sea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional scalings to relate geometry and forces to fluid rise/fall behavior in hydraulic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to bellows
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to bellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate bellows dimensions and compression ratios to airflow/pressure output by proportional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to commodity pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the prices of several commodities, as masts, diamonds, large timber, amber, loadstones, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional reasoning to relate size/quality/rarity to market value, with caution about economic complexities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to mill-dams, sea-banks, fortifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to mill-dams, sea banks, and the bulwarks or walls of fortresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale defensive/containment structures' strength and efficacy using proportional relations of dimensions and loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/sub-duplicate proportion applies to compression of elastic bodies and air in diving vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the compression of wool and other elastic bodies, and of the air within diving vessels, as also in the effects of screw-presses upon several materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model compressive response using proportional relations between applied force and deformation/pressure in elastic or confined systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: measuring refraction of the air
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for measuring the refraction of the air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/assess instrument capability for precise refraction measurements (sensitivity, angular resolution, calibration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: regulating places of fixed stars and planets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for regulating the places of the fixed stars and of the planets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument must provide accurate celestial coordinates (position measurements) with sufficient precision for star catalogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: stating latitude of places
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for stating the latitude of places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument must permit accurate determination of latitude (angular measurements of celestial bodies relative to horizon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: examining influences of planets on the earth
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for examining the influences of the planets on the earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide repeatable, precise positional data enabling study of planetary motions and hypothesized terrestrial influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: measuring the quantity of a degree upon the earth
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for measuring the quantity of a degree upon the earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument must support geodetic measurements—accurate angular measures over terrestrial baselines to determine a degree's arc length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: measuring seen distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for measuring seen distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable accurate angular-distance measurements (e.g., triangulation) for surveying and range determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: levelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for levelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument stability and alignment features must be sufficient for precise leveling tasks in surveying and timekeeping contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant use: taking diameters of sun, moon, and planets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new quadrant for taking the diameters of the sun, moon, and other planets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument must achieve fine angular resolution and accurate calibration to measure planetary/solar angular diameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary: instruments to take diameters to seconds and to observe the sun safely
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention of two other instruments: one for taking diameters to seconds; the other for looking on the body of the sun without injury to the eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized instruments or attachments should be designed to extend measurement precision (to arc-seconds) and to permit safe solar observation (attenuation/projection methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-operative sounding as proof of stone removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence for the success of a stone-cutting operation: 'his proofs are more than convincing, when at the end of three days, upon sounding, a stone is found in some, and none in others.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic post-operative examination (sounding) at specified timepoints (three days) to confirm presence or absence of calculi as objective evidence of treatment outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic observation: sample preparation and layered description
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopy practice: prepare/section ocular tissues (pierce cornea, dry cornea, cut crystalline humour, view vitreous and tunicles), report observations such as crystalline globules, layers of globules, filamentous particles, cavities in nerves, and coloration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specimen preparation method and observed microstructure in detail (appearance, arrangement of globules/filaments, cavities); compare several tissue layers and multiple samples for consistency.
